draft.headline: NQ falls 0.93% as Alphabet drags tech; yields ease
draft.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 0.93% with the US open minutes away, and headlines point to a record post-earnings drop in Alphabet. Yields are lower, which usually helps tech, but the tech-specific selling is the bigger force this morning.
draft.what_it_means: Alphabet's earnings miss is the main headline for tech: reports say the stock faces a record post-earnings loss, and that AI is starting to bite into search. Reports also say Google and Microsoft held off raising AI spending forecasts. Separately, the GDP headline showed the US economy grew a better-than-expected 3.4% in the third quarter while September inflation accelerated — strong growth, but hotter prices, a harder mix for the Fed.
draft.market_reaction: NQ is at 29,700.00, down 0.93% today and 279.50 points below the prior settle of 29,979.50. It sits just 19.25 points above yesterday's low of 29,680.75 and below the overnight high of 29,789.75. S&P 500 futures are only 0.28% lower. The session range is 306 points, 62% of a typical day's 494 points.
draft.rates_read: The 10-year yield is 4.993%, down 5.2 basis points today; the 2-year is 4.681%, down 5.4. Both are also lower over the past week, and the curve is +31bp, a normal shape. Falling yields usually help Nasdaq stocks because future profits are discounted less. Today that help is not enough to offset the tech-specific selling.
watch_next: Amazon earnings after the close; EPS forecast $2.01
Yesterday's low of 29,680.75, just under current NQ
September inflation detail inside the GDP report
draft.learn: A basis point (bp) is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so yields are quoted in tiny units. Small moves matter: a few basis points on the 10-year shifts borrowing costs across the economy and nudges how investors value future tech profits.
